# Region Sjælland — Sjælland

In the context of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB) national clinical quality reports, **Region Sjælland** and **Sjælland** represent two sides of the same geographic and administrative coin. Region Sjælland is the administrative organization responsible for healthcare delivery, data reporting, and formal feedback to the database. Sjælland refers to the geographical and statistical region itself—one of the five regions of [[danmark|Danmark]]—which encompasses the local hospitals where acute surgical care is actually performed. 

## Healthcare Infrastructure
The region's acute surgical data is aggregated from several major hospital units. According to the database's reporting structures, Sjælland contains [[holbaek-sygehus|Holbæk Sygehus]], [[nykoebing-f-sygehus|Nykøbing F Sygehus]], [[naestved-slagese-og-ringsted-sygehuse|Næstved, Slagelse og Ringsted sygehuse]], [[hospitalerne-i-nordsjaelland|Hospitalerne i Nordsjælland]], and [[sjaellands-universitetshospital|Sjællands Universitetshospital]] [^src9] [^src11]. Notably, [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] also appears in the region's specific data breakdowns for certain metrics, likely reflecting cross-regional patient flows or specialized treatment pathways rather than geographic location [^src11].

## Performance on Key Indicators
The region's performance is tracked across multiple clinical indicators over consecutive reporting periods. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], Sjælland achieved a fulfillment rate of 32.7% (95% CI: 28.6–36.9) during the 01.09.2022–31.08.2023 period [^src8]. This performance improved in the subsequent year, reaching 36.3% (95% CI: 32.3–40.4) for the 01.09.2023–31.08.2024 period [^src13]. 

Other indicators highlight regional disparities across Denmark. For [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], results varied nationally, with Region Sjælland recording 25.9% compared to [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] at 41.8% [^src14]. Similarly, for [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]], the proportion ranged from 15.7% in Region Sjælland to 19.6% in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src15]. In another metric (indikator 5y), Region Sjælland showed a rate of 10.6% [^src1].

## Data Quality and Supplementary Metrics
Data quality remains a focal point for the AKDB. For [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], the proportion of patients missing information varied significantly across the country, from a low of 1% in Region Sjælland to 15% in Region Midtjylland [^src4]. 

Supplementary clinical metrics provide further insight into acute surgical outcomes in the region. For the supplementary indicator [[indikator-5x]], 19.9% of patients in Region Sjælland were operated on within 6 hours for conditions such as perforation, ischemia, or bleeding [^src9]. Furthermore, 30-day mortality for patients undergoing acute surgery with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]] was recorded at 15.6% (28 out of 180 patients) [^src11].

## Demographics and Administrative Context
When comparing patient demographics and baseline health across the five Danish regions, supplemental analyses demonstrate that there are no significant differences in patient [[alder]] (age) [^src12] or [[asa-score|ASA]] scores [^src12] between Sjælland and regions like [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt]], [[midtjylland-region-i-alt]], [[nordjylland-region-i-alt]], and [[syddanmark-region-i-alt]]. 

Administratively, Region Sjælland actively participates in the database's governance. In response to the 2023 annual report for the Akut Kirurgi Databasen, the organization formally submitted no comments or remarks [^src2].
